28.11.2022 (Clause 31) AWARD 1.
This is a claim petition U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988, filed by petitioners.
The facts of the case are that on 25.02.2008 at about 03.55 A.M at Sadar Bazar to IOC Road side, Road No.629, Transport Coy Gate, P.S Delhi Cantt South West District, Delhi.

entities.text: P.S Delhi Cantt South West District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The driver of the offending bus bearing No. DL1P A1879 had parked the offending vehicle without giving any indication or signal and without obeying traffic rules and norms in a rash and negligent manner in no parking zone without caring for the other traffic on the road.

The deceased who was coming on his on his motor cycle bearing No.DL9S N2020 as per traffic rules and regulation and in a process the motor cycle of the deceased got struck/dashed with the offending bus.
As a result of which the deceased sustained multiple grievous injuries over his body.
The deceased was taken to Safdarjung Hospital, N Delhi where he was declared as brought dead.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place,
due to rash and negligent parking by Driver of offending bus.
The offending vehicle was owned by Manoj Kumar ( respondent No.1/ owner) and was insured with M/S National Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).

The petitioners have filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs.
25,00,000/ ( Twenty Five Lacs ) from respondents as compensation, alongwith interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
3. The respondent No.1 has filed his W.S stating therein that it was the deceased who was driving his motor cycle in rash and negligent act and hit the parked/stationed bus.
4. The respondent no. 2 (insurance company) has filed its written statement and denied the contents of averment made in para No.8 and 9 of the petition.
It is stated that offending vehicle was insured with the it.
It is stated that the alleged offending vehicle was not having a valid permit at the time of accident.

5. After completion of the proceedings, following issues were framed on 07.01.2013 as under:
(i) Whether Sh Radhey Shyam sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 25.08.2008due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.DL1PA1879 by R1 ? OPP.
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?
OPP.
(iii) Relief.
6.
In order to prove their claim, petitioners have examined petitioner Dhanshira as PW3.
PW1 Sh Ravinder Kumar Senior Manager
Hotel Excelsior Ltd.
PW2 HC Bijender and PW4 HC Himmat Dhanshira vs Manoj Kumar on 21 January, 2023

7. I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioners and respondents.
I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submission made by them and I also perused the record.

My issue wise findings are as under:
(i) Whether Sh Radhey Shyam sustained fatal injuries in a motor vehicle accident dated on 25.08.2008 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.DL1PA1879 by R1 ? OPP.
8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

To prove this fact petitioners examined PW3 Smt Dhansira , who has deposed that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent of R.1 who has parked the offending vehicle without observing the traffic rules and norms.
PW 2 HC Bijender has proved the copy of FIR Ex PW2/1.
The aforesaid witnesses have been duly cross examined but the testimony of the these PWs with respect to accident and rash & negligent parking of offending vehicle could not be impeached.
Moreover the proof of negligence, while disposing off a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/338/304A of IPC.

So far as the act of contributory negligence is concerned the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Javeri V Karamsey Kunvargi Tak, (2002) 6 SCC 455 has held that contributory negligence has to be proved, or, to say so, at the very least, shown by adducing evidence".

entities.text: Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Javeri V Karamsey Kunvargi Tak, (2002) 6 SCC 455
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents have not led any evidence or examined any witness to show the contributory negligence on the part of deceased.
The R2W2 has placed on record the investigation report Ex R2W2/1 in which it was surfaced that the offending vehicle was parked in no parking zone.
The site plan does not show that any parking indication was there near the parking of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered and it becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that the deceased was at fault, in any way.

The Hon'ble High Court of Andhra Prakesh has also not considered the contributory negligence in similar fact in case titled Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd Vs Bhupathi Sujatha & ors in M.A.C.M.A No.2717 of 2018.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd Vs Bhupathi Sujatha & ors in M.A.C.M.A No.2717 of 2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. The fact that Radhey Shyam died in that accident is also supported by his postmortem report on the dead body of victim.
Considering all the evidence as discussed above, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent parking of offending vehicle thereby causing death of Radhey Shyam.

10. This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that victim Radhey Shyam died in a motor vehicle accident due negligence on the respondent no.1 who had stationed the offending vehicle in the road side without any indication, parking lights or any other precautions.
ISSUE No.2: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, what amount and from whom?

Petitioner no.1 and 2 are the mother and father of victim ( deceased Radhey Shyam) as such LRs of victim.
12. Now coming to the extent of compensation.

According to the petitioners, at the time of accident,
the deceased Radhey Shyam was working as Chef at Hotel Excelsior Limited and as per pay slip Ex PW1/2 he was drawing a salary of Rs.14,296/
Ld Counsel for the petitioners as well Ld Counsel for R.2 has not disputed the salary slip Ex PW1/2.
As such the monthly income of deceased was Rs.14,296/ p.m at the time of accident.

13. As per the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others of Hon'ble Supreme Court the net income of the deceased is to be counted after deduction of tax and future benefit have to be given @ 40%.

sentences.text: 14. Keeping in view the fact that the age of the deceased was 31 years old ( 21.10.1977) The deceased was Bachelor at the time of accident so deceased spending 50% of his income on his personal expenses.

Therefore the income for the purpose of loss of dependency has to be taken as Rs.
10,007.20/ (14,296/ + 5,718.40  10,007.20) per month.
15. To calculate loss of dependency, the multiplier has to be taken on the basis of age of deceased.
A multiplier of 16 is thus taken in calculating loss of dependency.
Counting in this way, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 19,21,382.40 ( 10,007.20/ x 12 x 16).

This amount of Rs. 19,21,382.40/ (
In lumb sum Rs.19,21,500/) is allowed to petitioner no.1 and 2 as loss of dependency.

16. Apart from amount mentioned above, petitioner no. 1 is also granted a sum of Rs.16,500/ for funeral expenses, Rs.16,500/ for loss of estate and Rs. 44,000/ each to the petitioners for loss of consortium making a total sum of Rs. 20,42,500/
Detail of the whole award amount is: i. Loss of dependency Rs. 19,21,500/ ii. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/

iii . Loss of Estate Rs. 16,500/ v.
Loss of consortium Rs. 88,000/-
44,000/ each to the petitioner Total Rs. 20,42,500/
17.
Now coming to the extent of liability.

It has already been held herein above that the deceased died due to rash and negligent of R.1 who has stationed the offending vehicle in the road side without any indication, parking lights or any other precautions.
He is primarily liable to make payment.
However, the petitioners have made the respondent no. 2 (insurance company) as one of the party seeking direction to respondent no. 2 that it be directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.2 on the date of accident.
However, counsel for respondent no.2 has contended that it is not liable to pay any compensation as the the permit of the offending vehicle was not valid at the time of accident.
To prove this fact R.2 has not produced any evidence on record.
R.2 has not examined any concerned officer from the office of RTO/MLO.
R2 has examined RW1 Sh Amit Dabas an official of State Transport Audthority, who has deposed that the record pertaining to the offending vehicle is not available with respect to the date of accident.
So in the absence of any evidence on record the Tribunal can not presume that there was no permit of the offending vehicle.

7 of the petitioners fully supports their case, therefore, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against respondents by holding that petitioners are entitled for compensation from respondent no.2.
